findings.documented: Every request must carry api_key as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=...
findings.actual: API key passed in query parameter returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized with detail 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'. Key must be sent in X-API-Key request header.
findings.how_found: Issued GET /v1/listings with api_key query parameter as documented and received 401 response instructing header usage.
findings.impact: High - All query-parameter authenticated requests fail with 401 Unauthorized until converted to X-API-Key header.

findings.documented: Returns token object { token, token_type: 'Bearer', expires_in: 86400, user }. Tokens valid for 24h with no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Returns access_token instead of token, short 900s (15 min) expires_in, refresh_token, and refresh_url: '/auth/refresh'. User object omits name field.
findings.how_found: Sent POST /auth/login with valid demo credentials and inspected JSON response keys.
findings.impact: High - Client authentication logic referencing data.token or assuming 24h validity without refresh handling fails after 15 minutes.

findings.documented: Pagination uses 1-indexed page parameter and limit parameter up to 200. Response includes page, page_size, and total.
findings.actual: API completely ignores page parameter (always returns offset=0 unless offset is passed). Server caps limit at 50 max (limit=200 returns limit=50). Response contains limit, offset, count, total, has_more instead of page/page_size.
findings.how_found: Tested GET /v1/listings?page=2&limit=200 and observed offset=0, limit=50 in response object.
findings.impact: High - Requesting page=2 without offset returns duplicate page 1 data endlessly. Requesting limit=200 receives only 50 items.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings in the same locality and bedroom count.
findings.actual: Endpoint does not exist and returns HTTP 404 Not Found detail 'Not Found'.
findings.impact: Medium - Frontend similar listings recommendation section must be generated client-side or omitted.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites, and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} manage saved listings server side.
findings.actual: All /v1/favourites endpoints return HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.how_found: Issued GET, POST, and DELETE requests to /v1/favourites with valid bearer token.
findings.impact: High - Saved listings / favorites feature must be implemented using robust browser localStorage persistence.

findings.documented: Document states there is no refresh flow for authentication tokens.
findings.actual: Endpoint POST /auth/refresh exists and accepts refresh_token to issue a new access_token.
findings.how_found: Inspected POST /auth/login response which returned refresh_url: '/auth/refresh' and tested calling it.
findings.impact: Medium - Allows maintaining long-running user sessions without forcing full re-login every 15 minutes.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are integers in Indian rupees everywhere in the API (e.g., 8900000, 21400000).
findings.actual: price_min and price_max in /v1/projects are floating-point numbers in Crores (for values <= ~10) or Lakhs (for values > ~10). E.g. price_max: 99.8 (Lakhs) and 3.78 (Crores).
findings.how_found: Harvested /v1/projects and inspected price_min/price_max fields against associated listing prices.
findings.impact: High - Displaying raw project prices without unit conversion displays 99.8 rupees instead of 99.8 Lakhs (₹99,80,000) or 3.78 Crores (₹3,78,000,00).

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings includes inactive/withdrawn listings where boolean field is_live is false (827 inactive listings out of 3900 total records).
findings.how_found: Filtered harvested listings by is_live === false and found 827 inactive records.
findings.impact: High - Frontend must filter listings by is_live === true to prevent presenting inactive properties to buyers.

findings.documented: total_listings in /v1/projects is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with GET /v1/listings?project_id=...
findings.actual: total_listings in /v1/projects disagrees with the actual count of listings referencing that project_id for 332 out of 450 projects.
findings.how_found: Cross-referenced total_listings in /v1/projects against listings grouped by project_id in /v1/listings.
findings.impact: Medium - UI showing project listing counts must compute counts dynamically from active listings rather than relying on project metadata.

findings.documented: Timestamps are ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: posted_at timestamps in /v1/listings and /v1/rentals omit the explicit Z suffix or offset indicator (e.g. '2026-01-19T12:56:00').
findings.how_found: Inspected raw string values of posted_at in harvested listing records.
findings.impact: Medium - Date parsers assuming local timezone instead of IST (+05:30) produce incorrect date calculations.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Contains 25 corrupt records describing physically impossible states (negative price, super_built_up_area < carpet_area, floor > total_floors).
findings.how_found: Analyzed physical constraints across all 3900 listings in listings.json.
findings.impact: High - Displaying corrupt listings breaks UI layouts and distorts market statistics unless sanitized.

findings.documented: Every listing corresponds to a genuine sale property in your city.
findings.actual: Contains 24 fraudulent listings created to bait users with impossibly low prices (< ₹20,000) or advance-fee scam text ('Site visit only after the booking amount is paid').
findings.how_found: Scanned descriptions for scam phrases and prices for bait thresholds.
findings.impact: High - Fraudulent listings must be flagged or filtered to protect users from advance-fee scams.

findings.documented: Each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Harvesting all pages yields 3900 records describing 3875 unique physical properties. 25 physical properties have duplicate listing records across different websites/agents.
findings.how_found: Deduplicated listing records by physical property keys (locality, apartment_name, bedroom, bathroom, floor, carpet_area).
findings.impact: Medium - Search results contain duplicate listings for the same apartment unit across different platforms.
